entries.final_answer: starlight-openapi first, per ADR-0049. A WP01 spike checks OpenAPI 3.1, content entries, theme tokens and byte-stable rebuilds. If it doesn't fit, the fallback is our own build-time Markdown generator, recorded in a new ADR. Redoc is rejected: standalone page, JS-only content, loose CSP, its own dark-mode class, telemetry.

entries.final_answer: Yes. In: two or more versions, a list-of-links switcher, a text unreleased badge, the raw spec byte-identical plus sha256, fail-closed errors, how-to and CSP note, opt-in with no install cost. Out: per-operation search, llms.txt operation summary, dropdown switcher, tagged archive, multi-file $ref, and the 0.6.0 release (cut separately after merge).

entries.final_answer: Accept injected routes. Wire the llms.txt version list (FR-008). Exempt generated API routes from the frontmatter gate. Record the agent API, the content graph and glossary autolinking as follow-ups in the ADR (FR-013). Routes alone do not trigger the fallback.
entries.question: If the spike finds starlight-openapi injects routes (no content entries), is that acceptable with gaps wired or listed, or does it trigger the own-generator fallback?

entries.final_answer: Waive narrowly and keep starlight-openapi. API pages may add only the pinned plugin's known inline scripts; a gate pins their hashes and fails on any new one. Code samples are off (1 script). The how-to documents the hashes. Add the description adapter and the stylesheet filter. The ADR-0049 addendum records the waiver and moves it to Accepted.

entries.final_answer: reference/api, so pages are at /reference/api/<label>/. A configured section is checked against reserved and authored routes.
